record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: In online graph coloring, vertices arrive sequentially and must be colored irrevocably based only on the subgraph seen so far. A graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if some online coloring algorithm has its color usage bounded by a function of chi_OL(G), the optimal online chromatic number of each graph G. Is the class of graphs that are both triangle-free and P6-free, equivalently (C3, P6)-free graphs, online chi_OL-bounded?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14 Is the class of (C3, P6)-free graphs on-line χOL-bounded?
We denote the path and cycle on n vertices by Pn and Cn, respectively.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the online graph coloring model, the vertices of a graph are revealed one at a time in some adversarial order. When a vertex v is revealed, all edges between v and previously revealed vertices are also revealed, and the online algorithm must irrevocably assign v a proper color (different from the colors already given to its revealed neighbors), based only on the induced subgraph seen so far. For a graph G, let χ_OL(G) denote the online chromatic number of G, that is, the minimum over all online coloring algorithms A of the maximum, over all presentation orders of V(G), of the number of colors used by A on G.

A class C of graphs is said to be online χ_OL-bounded if there exists a function f: ℕ → ℕ and an online coloring algorithm A such that for every graph G ∈ C and every presentation order of V(G), the algorithm A uses at most f(χ_OL(G)) colors.

For an integer n ≥ 1, let P_n denote the path on n vertices and C_n the cycle on n vertices. A graph G is called (C_3, P_6)-free if it contains neither C_3 nor P_6 as an induced subgraph (equivalently, G is triangle-free and induced-P_6-free).

Question: Is the class of (C_3, P_6)-free graphs online χ_OL-bounded?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published resolution of online χ_OL-boundedness for (C_3, P_6)-free graphs. Known results address the offline chromatic number (Randerath et al. showed χ ≤ 4 for (C_3, P_6)-free graphs) and offline/poly-time coloring for P_6-free graphs, but the online version for this specific class appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Perfect coloring and linearly chi-bound P_6-Free graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Randerath et al. proved that every (P_6,C_3)-free graph G satisfies χ(G) ≤ 4.
status_evidence.claim: Offline chromatic number for this class is bounded, but this does not address the online version.

status_evidence.title: 3-Colorability ∈ P for P6-free graphs
status_evidence.snippet: 3-colorability is in P for P6-free graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature focuses on offline coloring, not online χ_OL-boundedness.
